senses.en: make worse

examples.text: The proposed shutdown would exacerbate unemployment problems.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exacerbāre(몹시 쓰게 하다, 자극하다)에서 왔습니다. 쓴맛을 더해 상황을 더 나쁘게 만든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: severe and unremitting in making demands

examples.text: The conductor was an exacting taskmaster who made the orchestra repeat each passage dozens of times.

senses.en: requiring precise accuracy

examples.text: Restoring the fresco was an exacting task that demanded years of patient, precise work.

senses.en: praise, glorify, or honor

examples.text: They exalted their queen.

senses.en: raise in rank, character, or status

examples.text: The man was exalted from a humble carpenter to a minister.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exaltāre(높이 들어 올리다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 높이 올려 칭송한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To tax the patience of; irk, frustrate, vex, provoke, annoy; to make angry.

examples.text: The constant delays and contradictory instructions began to exasperate even the most patient members of the committee.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exasperāre(거칠게 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 신경을 거칠게 긁어 화나게 한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: greatly annoyed; out of patience

examples.text: Exasperated by the third cancelled flight, she demanded to speak with the airline's manager.

senses.en: To cut out; to remove.

examples.text: Military censors have excised some details from the photographs for security reasons.

senses.en: A tax charged on goods produced within the country (as opposed to customs duties, charged on goods from outside the country).

examples.text: The government raised the excise on tobacco and alcohol to help close the budget deficit.

origin.ko: 라틴어 excīdere(잘라 내다)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 도려내듯 잘라 삭제한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To strongly condemn or criticize.

examples.text: The editorial excoriated the minister for ignoring repeated warnings about the unsafe bridge.

senses.en: tear or wear off the skin or make sore by abrading

examples.text: The rough harness excoriated the horse's flanks after a long day of hauling.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 excoriāre(가죽을 벗기다)에서 왔습니다. 껍질을 벗기듯 통렬하게 비난한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: extremely painful
senses.ko: 극심한 고통을 주는, 견딜 수 없는

examples.text: After the accident he endured weeks of excruciating pain before the surgery finally brought relief.

origin.ko: 라틴어 excruciāre(고문하다)에서 왔고, cruc은 '십자가'입니다. 십자가형 같은 고통이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: pronounce not guilty of criminal charges

examples.text: New DNA evidence exculpated the defendant after he had spent twelve years in prison.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 exculpāre에서 왔습니다. culpa(죄)를 밖으로 내보내 혐의를 벗긴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unequivocally detestable

examples.text: Historians condemned the regime for its execrable treatment of political prisoners.

senses.en: of very poor quality or condition

examples.text: The critics agreed that the restaurant's service was execrable and its food barely edible.

origin.ko: 라틴어 execrābilis에서 왔습니다. 신성한 곳에서 저주받아 쫓겨날 만한 '혐오스러운'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: find repugnant

examples.text: Many citizens execrated the dictator long before his regime finally collapsed.

senses.en: To declare to be hateful or abhorrent; to denounce.

examples.text: The crowd gathered outside the courthouse to execrate the officials who had approved the scheme.

origin.ko: 라틴어 execrārī(저주하다)에서 왔습니다. 대상을 저주받은 것으로 선언한다는 데서 몹시 혐오한다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: A critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially a religious text.

examples.text: Her doctoral thesis offered a detailed exegesis of the book of Job.

origin.ko: 그리스어 exḗgēsis(설명, 해석)에서 왔습니다. 글의 뜻을 밖으로 이끌어 내는 일입니다.

senses.en: Something fit to be imitated; an ideal, a worthy model or role model: a desirable example.

examples.text: Michelangelo's "David" is an exemplar of Renaissance sculpture.

senses.en: Something typical or representative; an example that typifies its class.

examples.text: The novel is often cited as an exemplar of the nineteenth-century social realism that followed.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exemplar(본보기)에서 왔습니다. 여러 가지 중 뽑아 놓은 견본이라 모범이 됩니다.

senses.en: clarify by giving an example of

examples.text: The professor used a famous court case to exemplify how precedent shapes legal reasoning.

senses.en: be typical of

examples.text: Her quiet generosity exemplifies the community spirit that the town is known for.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exemplum(본보기)에서 중세 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 본보기를 들어 보인다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: put to use

examples.text: He considered exerting his influence on John to gain an advantage for himself.

senses.en: make a great effort at a mental or physical task

examples.text: She exerted herself to finish the manuscript before the publisher's deadline.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exserere(밖으로 내밀다)에서 왔습니다. 힘을 밖으로 밀어내 쓰는 데서 '행사하다'가 되었습니다.

senses.en: use of physical or mental energy; hard work

examples.text: The climb required such exertion that several members of the group had to turn back.

senses.en: performed comprehensively and completely; not superficial or partial

examples.text: The committee conducted an exhaustive review of the agency's records before issuing its findings.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 exhaustīvus에서 왔습니다. 속을 남김없이 퍼내듯 빠짐없이 다룬다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: making lively and cheerful

examples.text: Hiking to the summit at dawn was an exhilarating experience that none of us will forget.

origin.ko: 라틴어 hilaris(즐거운)에서 온 exhilarate에 -ing이 붙었습니다. 기분을 확 들뜨게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To urge; to advise earnestly.

examples.text: The coach exhorted his exhausted players to give everything they had in the final quarter.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exhortārī(격려하다)에서 왔습니다. 곁에서 힘껏 부추겨 행동을 권한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a sudden unforeseen crisis (usually involving danger) that requires immediate action

examples.text: The mayor invoked special powers to deal with the exigency created by the flood.

senses.en: that which is required in a particular situation — usually used in plural.

examples.text: The trench maps used in the Great War resulted from the exigencies of war.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exigere(요구하다)에서 왔습니다. 당장 대처를 요구하는 긴급 상황입니다.

senses.en: Urgent; pressing; needing immediate action.

examples.text: Doctors had to act quickly because of the exigent circumstances surrounding the patient's collapse.

senses.en: Demanding; requiring great effort.

examples.text: The exigent standards of the guild forced apprentices to practice for years before earning recognition.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exigere(요구하다)의 현재분사에서 왔습니다. 즉각적 행동을 요구하는 '긴급한'입니다.

senses.en: the quality of being meager

examples.text: The exiguity of the villagers' food supplies became obvious as the harsh winter dragged on.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 exiguitās에서 중세 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 아주 적고 보잘것없는 상태를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: To free (someone) from accusation or blame.

examples.text: The investigation exonerated the pilot, concluding that mechanical failure had caused the crash.

senses.en: To free (someone) from an obligation, responsibility or task.

examples.text: The new contract exonerated the tenants from any liability for damage caused by the storm.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exonerāre(짐을 내려놓다)에서 왔습니다. 죄의 짐을 벗겨 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Exceeding proper limits; excessive or unduly high; extravagant.

examples.text: You also have to pay exorbitant interest if you have credit card debt.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 exorbitāre(바퀴 자국에서 벗어나다)에서 왔습니다. 정상 궤도를 벗어난 '터무니없는'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To drive out (an evil spirit) from a person, place or thing, especially by an incantation or prayer.

examples.text: The priest attempted to exorcise the evil spirit from the house.

origin.ko: 그리스어 exorkízō(맹세로 묶다, 악령을 쫓다)에서 왔습니다. 맹세의 힘으로 악령을 밖으로 몰아낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: being or from or characteristic of another place or part of the world

examples.text: The market was filled with exotic fruits that most of the tourists had never tasted.

senses.en: strikingly strange or unusual

examples.text: Physicists have proposed exotic forms of matter that behave unlike anything seen in ordinary experiments.

origin.ko: 그리스어 exōtikós(바깥에서 온)에서 왔습니다. 바깥, 곧 외국에서 온 '이국적인' 것을 가리킵니다.

senses.en: Talkative and sociable.

examples.text: After a glass of wine the usually reserved host grew expansive and told stories for hours.

senses.en: Comprehensive in scope or extent.

examples.text: The historian's expansive study traces trade routes across three continents over a thousand years.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expandere(펼치다)에서 왔습니다. 마음을 활짝 펼친 듯 개방적이고 말이 많다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To write or speak at length; to be copious in argument or discussion.

examples.text: The professor expatiated on the causes of the war for nearly an hour without notes.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expatiārī(널리 거닐다)에서 왔습니다. 말이 넓게 돌아다니듯 길게 늘어놓는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a person who is voluntarily absent from home or country

examples.text: Many expatriates in the city gather weekly to share news and meals from home.

senses.en: expel from a country

examples.text: The regime expatriated several prominent writers who had criticized the government in print.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 expatriāre(조국 밖으로 내보내다)에서 왔습니다. 조국(patria)을 떠나 사는 사람입니다.

senses.en: Affording short-term benefit, often at the expense of the long-term.

examples.text: The council chose the expedient solution of borrowing more money rather than reforming the budget.

senses.en: Suitable to effect some desired end or the purpose intended.

examples.text: Most people, faced with a decision, will choose the most expedient option.

senses.en: a means to an end; not necessarily a principled or ethical one

examples.text: Critics called the tax cut a political expedient designed to win votes before the election.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expedīre(발을 풀어 앞으로 내보내다)에서 왔습니다. 거치적거림이 없어 당장 유리하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: speed up the progress of; facilitate

examples.text: He expedited the search by alphabetizing the papers.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expedīre(발의 족쇄를 풀다)에서 왔습니다. 걸림돌을 치워 일을 빠르게 진행시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: make amends for

examples.text: He spent the rest of his life working in hospitals to expiate the guilt of his youth.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expiāre(속죄하다)에서 왔습니다. 잘못을 갚아 죄를 씻는다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Able to be explained.

examples.text: The strange readings were perfectly explicable once the technicians discovered the faulty sensor.

origin.ko: 라틴어 explicāre(펼치다)에서 왔습니다. 접힌 것을 펼쳐 보일 수 있으니 '설명할 수 있는'입니다.

senses.en: To explain meticulously or in great detail.

examples.text: My homework is to explicate a poem.

origin.ko: 라틴어 explicāre(펼치다)에서 왔습니다. 접혀 있던 뜻을 하나하나 펼쳐 설명한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: One who or that which explicates.

examples.text: As an explicator of medieval poetry, she made difficult verse accessible to generations of students.

senses.en: precisely and clearly expressed or readily observable; leaving nothing to implication

examples.text: I gave explicit instructions for him to stay here, but he followed me, anyway.

origin.ko: 라틴어 explicitus(펼쳐진, 풀린)에서 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 접힌 곳 없이 활짝 펼쳐 분명하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: draw from; make good use of

examples.text: The company hopes to exploit new markets in Southeast Asia as demand grows.

senses.en: To make unfair use of someone else's labor, person, or property to one's own advantage.

examples.text: The factory owners exploited immigrant workers by paying them far less than the legal minimum wage.

senses.en: a notable achievement

examples.text: The first trek to the summit of Mount Everest was a stunning exploit.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 esploit(성과, 이용)에서 왔고, 라틴어 explicāre(펼치다)와 이어집니다. 자원을 펼쳐 활용한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: The improper use of something for selfish purposes.

examples.text: The report documented the systematic exploitation of migrant laborers on the plantations.

senses.en: the act of making some area of land or water more profitable or productive or useful

examples.text: The exploitation of the region's mineral wealth transformed a sleepy village into a bustling mining town.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 exploitation에서 왔고, exploit에 -ation이 붙었습니다. 남을 이용해 이익을 뽑아내는 것입니다.

senses.en: In the nature of exploitation; acting to exploit someone or something

examples.text: We are protesting the company's exploitative policies.

senses.en: One who expounds, represents or advocates.

examples.text: She was a leading exponent of free trade throughout her long political career.

senses.en: a mathematical notation indicating the number of times a quantity is multiplied by itself

examples.text: In the expression five cubed, the exponent tells you to multiply five by itself three times.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expōnere(밖에 내놓다, 설명하다)에서 왔습니다. 주장을 밖에 내세워 설명하는 사람입니다.

senses.en: the act of expressing earnest opposition or protest

examples.text: Despite his father's expostulation, the young man refused to abandon his plan to sail alone.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expostulāre(강하게 요구하다)에서 왔습니다. 잘못을 따져 간곡히 항의하는 것입니다.

senses.en: To set out the meaning of; to explain or discuss at length.

examples.text: Today I'll expound at length the theory propounded last week.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expōnere(밖에 내놓다)에서 고대 프랑스어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 뜻을 늘어놓아 설명한다는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: remove by erasing or crossing out or as if by drawing a line

examples.text: The judge ordered the juvenile conviction expunged from the defendant's permanent record.

senses.en: To eliminate completely; to annihilate.

examples.text: The new regime tried to expunge every trace of the old order from public memory.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expungere(점을 찍어 지우다)에서 왔습니다. 고대에 지울 글자 아래 점을 찍어 표시한 데서 온 말입니다.

senses.en: To edit out (incorrect, offensive, or otherwise undesirable information) from a book or other publication; to cleanse; to purge.

examples.text: The publisher decided to expurgate the love scene from the book, to make it more child-friendly.

origin.ko: 라틴어 expurgāre(깨끗이 씻어 내다)에서 왔습니다. 글에서 불온한 부분을 씻어 낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: still in existence; not extinct or destroyed or lost

examples.text: There are many narrow-gauge systems still extant.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extāre(밖으로 서 있다, 존재하다)에서 왔습니다. 사라지지 않고 우뚝 남아 있다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: with little or no preparation or forethought

examples.text: The senator abandoned her script and gave a moving extemporaneous speech to the crowd.

origin.ko: 라틴어 ex tempore(그때그때)에서 후기 라틴어를 거쳐 왔습니다. 준비 없이 그 순간에 즉흥으로 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: perform without preparation

examples.text: he extemporized a speech at the wedding

origin.ko: 라틴어 ex tempore(즉석에서)에 -ize가 붙었습니다. 준비 없이 즉석에서 해 낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: lessen or to try to lessen the seriousness or extent of

examples.text: His lawyer argued that the defendant's youth and difficult upbringing should extenuate the offense.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extenuāre(얇게 만들다)에서 왔습니다. 죄의 무게를 얇게 줄여 경감한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: partially excusing or justifying

examples.text: Because of extenuating circumstances, the committee agreed to accept the application after the deadline.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extenuāre(얇게 하다)의 현재분사형입니다. 사정을 참작해 책임을 줄여 준다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: praise, glorify, or honor

examples.text: Reviewers extolled the novel's elegant prose and its unflinching portrait of rural poverty.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extollere(높이 들어 올리다)에서 왔습니다. 높이 들어 올려 칭송한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: obtain by coercion or intimidation

examples.text: They extorted money from the executive by threatening to reveal his past to the company boss

origin.ko: 라틴어 extorquēre(비틀어 짜내다)에서 왔습니다. 상대를 비틀어 억지로 빼앗아 내는 이미지입니다.

senses.en: not pertinent to the matter under consideration

examples.text: The editor deleted several extraneous details that distracted readers from the central argument.

senses.en: Not essential or intrinsic.

examples.text: The architect stripped away every extraneous ornament, leaving a clean and functional facade.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extrāneus(바깥에서 온)에서 왔습니다. 문제 바깥에 있어 관련이 없다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: To infer by extending known information.

examples.text: Economists extrapolated from last year's figures to predict that growth would slow considerably.

senses.en: To estimate the value of a variable outside a known range from values within that range by assuming that the estimated value follows logically from the known ones

examples.text: The researchers extrapolated the trend line beyond the measured data to estimate future temperatures.

origin.ko: 라틴어 extrā(바깥에)와 interpolate의 -polate를 합쳐 만든 말입니다. 아는 범위 밖까지 미루어 추정한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: unrestrained, especially with regard to feelings

examples.text: The advertisement made extravagant claims about the supplement's ability to cure every known illness.

senses.en: recklessly wasteful

examples.text: The heir's extravagant spending soon exhausted the fortune his grandfather had spent decades building.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 extravagārī(범위 밖을 헤매다)에서 왔습니다. 적정선을 벗어나 떠돈다는 데서 '과도한'이 되었습니다.

senses.en: joyously unrestrained

examples.text: The exuberant crowd poured into the streets to celebrate the team's first championship in decades.

senses.en: produced or growing in extreme abundance

examples.text: Exuberant vines covered the walls of the abandoned house and crept across its collapsed roof.

origin.ko: 라틴어 exūberāre(넘쳐흐르다)에서 왔습니다. uber는 젖통을 뜻해 젖이 넘치듯 활기가 넘친다는 이미지입니다.
